body:
## What this changes

Splitting a task was itself a task Formal AI could not do. Both halves of it —
"split this task into subtasks" and "is this task atomic?" — landed in the
unknown-prompt fallback, so nothing could drive the descent from "solve this
issue and open a PR" down to a step the engine can actually complete.

This PR makes decomposition a working task. The split answer and the atomicity
answer are **two views of one recursion**, produced by one call into
`src/task_decomposition.rs`, which is why they can never disagree: the
atomicity judgement *is* the recursion's base case.

Fixes #847.

## How it works

- **`src/task_decomposition.rs`** — the recursion. `decompose_task(task,
  max_depth)` splits a task on its sentence and conjunction boundaries,
  keeps only fragments with an observable completion criterion
  (`is_checkable`), and recurses into every non-atomic child until each leaf
  is atomic or the depth bound is reached. Every leaf records *why* it stopped
  (`AtomicityReason::{DirectMethod, SingleNeed, DepthBound, NotAtomic}`), so a
  truncated recursion is reported rather than hidden.
- **`src/solver_handlers/task_decomposition.rs`** — the handler. It classifies
  the prompt as one of three questions (atomicity, first step, split) and
  renders the same decomposition three ways.
- **Recognition is data, not Rust** (the #386 convention). All natural-language
  surfaces live in `data/seed/meanings-decomposition.lino` as role-tagged
  lexemes for en/ru/hi/zh, and all reply text in
  `data/seed/multilingual-responses-decomposition.lino`. The Rust side names
  only the language-neutral roles — there is no per-language phrase list in
  `src/`.
- **Routing** — `looks_like_task_decomposition` is exported so
  `intent_formalization` promotes `handler:task_decomposition` ahead of
  `handler:procedural_how_to`; the routing relevant and the handler therefore
  share one recogniser and cannot drift. `task_decomposition` also sits above
  `text_manipulation` in `data/seed/handler-precedence.lino`, so "split" reads
  as splitting a *task* rather than splitting a *string*.
- **Depth is configuration** — the contextual dispatch path passes the live
  `SolverConfig::max_decomposition_depth`, so lowering the bound is visible in
  the answer.
- **Sub-tasks are `sub_impulse` events** — `record_task_decomposition` appends
  one per sub-task, reusing the existing structure rather than inventing a
  parallel one, so each surfaces as a `sub_impulse:<id>` evidence link.

Relation to #699: recognition here is already data-driven (roles + seed
surfaces), but the handler still lives in the specialized dispatch table. When
#699 lands the meta-method surface, this handler is a direct candidate to move
onto it — nothing in the routing depends on its being a special case.

## Reproduction and measurement

Before (v0.303.0, `main`), both prompts refused:

```
$ ./target/release/formal-ai chat --silent --prompt "Split this coding task into at least two smaller independent subtasks ..."
I could not determine ... and cannot infer a verified answer.
```

After, via the issue's own harness:

```
$ ONLY=decomp experiments/issue_847_coding_ladder/run_coding_ladder.sh
PASS  decomp.split_two_part  L2
PASS  decomp.split_issue     L2
PASS  decomp.split_module    L2
PASS  decomp.is_atomic_yes   L3
PASS  decomp.is_atomic_no    L3
PASS  decomp.next_step       L3

TOTAL 6/6 passed
```

On the pre-PR binary those same six scored 2/6 (only the two questions the
old fallback happened to echo). Across the full 130-task ladder the branch
measures 45/130 (L1 0/16, L2 3/12, L3 4/28, L4 38/74), up from the v0.303.0
`main` baseline of 38/130; the deltas are exactly the decomposition surfaces
this PR adds — decomposition 2→6, knowledge 4→6, multilingual 3→4. Everything
else is unchanged, which is the intended blast radius: this PR teaches
recognition, not code generation.

Two harness-correctness fixes rode along, because a measurement you can't
trust is worse than none (`experiments/issue_847_coding_ladder`):
- L1 ("solve the issue and open a PR") was verified with
  `git branch -a | grep -q issue-N`, which counts remote-tracking refs — so a
  branch anyone had already pushed scored as work the agent just did (on the
  first Linux repeat that turned L1 into a phantom 7/16, one of them the branch
  the run itself was on). L1 now verifies through `new_branch_for.sh` against a
  ref snapshot taken immediately before each task.
- `formal-ai with agent` leaks a ~200 MB scratch home per task; once `/tmp`
  filled, the temporary server stopped starting and the tail of a long run
  measured nothing while recording FAILs. The runner now reclaims the scratch
  home after every task and reports a never-started server as NOT MEASURED,
  counted apart from a failure. This run had 0 NOT MEASURED.

## Tests

- `tests/unit/issue_847_task_decomposition.rs` — 7 reproduction tests, written
  against the exact prompts in the issue.
- `tests/unit/specification/task_decomposition.rs` — 11 specifications, one per
  acceptance-checklist line, with splitting and atomicity pinned in all four
  supported languages.
- `tests/unit/specification/method_registry.rs` — the contextual-override count
  moves from six to seven.

## Repository gates the new surfaces touched

Adding seed data and three `src/` modules moved four repository-wide gates,
all re-closed: total reference closure (`scripts/close-total.py` re-run), the
meaning-graph closure (`defined-by entity`, not the undefined `thing`), the
self-AST census (`regenerate_self_ast_census`), and the contextual-handler
count. Full local suite green: `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy
--all-targets --all-features -D warnings`, `cargo test --all-features`
(2765 passed, 0 failed), and `audit-total-closure.py` (0 unresolved).

Requirements R847-1 … R847-8 in `REQUIREMENTS.md` map each acceptance
checkbox to its implementation and its test.

## Self-hosting evidence

The decomposition fix and its tests are hand-authored maintenance and carry no
self-authorship trailers — an honest 0% is valid per `CONTRIBUTING.md`, which
forbids fabricating attribution. To keep the differential self-hosting ratchet
(`scripts/self-hosting-metric.rs`, the `evidence-check` job) honest *and* green,
one isolated commit records a **genuine** Formal AI session: a real Agent CLI
run driving the whole-repository source-to-links projection recipe, plus the
exhaustive `SourceLinks::owned()` rendering of all 301 owned modules (including
this branch's `src/task_decomposition.rs` and
`src/solver_handlers/task_decomposition.rs`), each proven to round-trip
byte-for-byte. Every line under
`docs/case-studies/issue-847/self-hosting-evidence/` is engine output;
`experiments/issue-847-self-hosting-evidence/run.sh` regenerates it
deterministically. The branch now measures 33.12% self-authored and the ratchet
holds against `main`.

commits.messageBody:
Decomposition is a working task like any other, so the surfaces that make
splitting, atomicity and first-step prompts recognisable belong in seed data
rather than in a per-language phrase list in Rust (issue #386 convention).

data/seed/meanings-decomposition.lino declares eight roles in English,
Russian, Hindi and Chinese. The observable/unobservable action pair is the
checkability oracle the acceptance list asks for: a sub-task is a valid child
only when a human can tell, by looking, whether it is done.

src/task_decomposition.rs is the algorithm those roles drive. Splitting a task
and judging whether it is atomic are two views of one recursion, so they share
one implementation: a task is atomic exactly when the splitter cannot produce
two independently checkable children from it. Recursion runs to a fixpoint
bounded by max_decomposition_depth, and the bound is reported rather than
hidden. Every node is recorded as a sub_impulse event, reusing the existing
event kind instead of inventing a parallel structure.
commits.messageHeadline: seed: add task-decomposition roles and surfaces for issue #847

commits.messageBody:
…handler

Issue #847: both halves of decomposition were refused, landing in the
unknown-prompt fallback. They are two views of one recursion, so they
share one handler and one call into task_decomposition: the atomicity
answer is the recursion's base case and the split answer is its result.

Recognition is role-driven per issue #386 — the splitting verbs, sub-task
nouns, atomicity predicates and reply text all live in the seed, with no
per-language phrase list in Rust. The handler is registered on both the
regular table (shipped default depth) and the contextual surface, so the
configured max_decomposition_depth reaches it and a truncated recursion
is reported instead of hidden.

has_depth_bound_leaf now uses the same unsplittable test as the row
renderer, so the depth-bound note and the row markers cannot disagree.
commits.messageHeadline: Route split-into-subtasks and is-it-atomic through one decomposition …

commits.messageBody:
…es opened

The new decomposition surfaces broke four repository-wide gates, each for a
different reason:

  * `meanings-decomposition.lino` used bare `#` header comments, which the
    total-closure audit reads as value tokens. Wrap the comment text in
    backticks, the convention the lexicon-import files already use, and
    re-run `scripts/close-total.py` so the seven new response intents and
    their 28 response ids are defined meanings.
  * The two new noun meanings pointed at `thing`, which is not a defined
    meaning; `entity` is the parent the rest of the seed uses for nouns.
  * The self-AST census had no documents for the three new modules.
  * Adding a contextual override makes seven, not six.
commits.messageHeadline: Close the seed and self-representation gates the decomposition surfac…

commits.messageBody:
Three defects, all found by running the full 130-task dataset on Linux
rather than the macOS box the committed baseline came from.

The agent CLI copies a ~200 MB scratch home into TMPDIR per invocation
and never removes it. At task 88 of 130 the temporary server stopped
coming up, and every remaining task recorded `exited before listening:
exit status: 101` as an ordinary FAIL -- 39 tasks of pure noise that
read as measurements. The scratch home is now reclaimed after each task,
and a task whose server never started is reported as NOT MEASURED and
counted separately, so an incomplete run announces itself.

`git checkout -- .` reverted experiments/ too, so a filtered re-run
(ONLY=...) silently discarded the previous full run's results.json. The
checkout now honours the same experiments/ exclusion `git clean` does.

Results are written after every task instead of only at the end, so an
interrupted half-hour run keeps what it measured.
commits.messageHeadline: Stop the ladder harness from fabricating results on a long run

commits.messageBody:
`git branch -a | grep -q issue-846` counts remote-tracking refs, so any
clone that has fetched the remote scores branches other people pushed as
work the agent just did. On the first Linux repeat of the 130-task run that
turned L1 from 0/16 into 7/16 with no engine change behind it -- one of the
seven was the branch the measurement itself was running from.

The runner now snapshots every ref immediately before launching a task and
new_branch_for.sh requires a match that is absent from that snapshot.
commits.messageHeadline: experiments: L1 must see a branch that appeared during the task

commits.messageBody:
Clean Linux run with the fixed harness (new_branch_for.sh, scratch reclaim,
0 NOT MEASURED). decomposition 6/6 -- this PR's contribution; the same six
scored 2/6 on the pre-PR binary. L1 holds at 0/16 under the corrected verify.

commits.messageBody:
The public doc for `SubTask::has_depth_bound_leaf` linked to the private
`Self::collect_rows`, which `rustdoc::private_intra_doc_links` rejects under
`-D warnings` — the exact flags CI's Lint and Format Check runs `cargo doc`
with. Local clippy/fmt/test never exercise `cargo doc`, so this slipped past.
Reworded to a plain code span; the doc reads the same.
commits.messageHeadline: Fix rustdoc: drop private intra-doc link in has_depth_bound_leaf
